NAME: Global Jurisdiction Reference Number
DESCRIPTION: The Global Jurisdiction Reference Number (GJRN) is administered by the International Bureau for Statistical Harmonization (IBSH), an intergovernmental body headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, whose website is www.ibsh.int. It is a numeric country identifier used in the international exchange of official statistics, replacing a patchwork of agency-specific country identifiers in census, trade and migration datasets. The GJRN was established by the Convention on Cross-Border Statistical Data Exchange, adopted in Geneva on 14 June 2021; it was phased in during 2022 and 2023 and has been mandatory for IBSH data submissions since 1 January 2024. Each participating sovereign state has exactly one GJRN code; 178 states participate. Every GJRN code is a three-digit number between 100 and 999; codes never have leading zeros, letters or check digits. Codes were allocated by lot, in a public draw held when each state acceded to the convention; they carry no geographic, alphabetical, sequential or regional meaning. A state's GJRN code is permanent: codes are never changed, reassigned or reused. GJRN codes are unrelated to telephone calling codes or any other country numbering system. The GJRN is used as the country key in statistical data submissions to the IBSH, in the REPORTER_GJRN field of IBSH interchange file headers, and on each country's page of the IBSH Statistical Portal.
